lead.headline: Anthropic IPO: VCs to make billions, Amazon set to make much more
lead.deck: Anthropic S-1 filed 26 October, on track for Nasdaq listing (ticker: ANT). $80.7B non-cash convertible-note revaluation. VCs take massive gains; Amazon eyes disproportionate infrastructure capture.
lead.summary: Anthropic files its IPO on the S-1. VCs raise $80.7B from convertible notes with mandatory repricing; Amazon positions for infrastructure scale. The AI economy enters a new phase — and regulators are watching.
lead.why: For executives, the IPO signals that AI is now a serious industrial player — not just a tech startup story.

body.t: Anthropic S-1, filed on 26 October, places the company on the path to a Nasdaq listing under the ANT symbol.
The $80.7 billion non-cash convertible note revaluation triggers massive nominal gains for early investors.
Q2 2026 revenue reached $16.3 billion with positive operating income, a first for the lab.
Amazon, quietly investing across the AI stack, is positioned to capture disproportionate value as Anthropic scales.
The IPO marks the transition from the 'capacity period' to the 'value period' in the AI industry.
US labs argue that AI development requires market-driven investment, not regulation, but the EU's approach is being watched closely worldwide.

articles.title: Google Genie 4: Audio and real-time world model
articles.takeaway: Genie 4 adds audio and real-time steering; world models extend into interactive 3D.

body.t: Google DeepMind unveiled Genie 4, a world model that generates realistic 3D environments with native audio.
The model maintains a consistent scene for two minutes and supports user control in real time.
Genie 4 demonstrates the next step in world models: moving from static generation to real-time interactive control.
World models bridge the gap between generation and interactive control, enabling new applications.
CEO of Google DeepMind acknowledges that real-time control remains experimental but shows strong promise.

articles.title: Delaware plan: AI agents to run entire businesses
articles.takeaway: Delaware proposes AI agents as legal entities — the first step toward fully autonomous corporate governance.

body.t: Delaware's new regulatory proposal would allow AI agents to run entire businesses without human oversight.
The plan proposes creating legal structures for AI agents to operate as entities with juridical personality.
This is the first time a US state has proposed regulatory frameworks for AI-managed companies.
The proposal could reshape corporate law, liability, and governance in the AI era.
Legal experts warn that AI agents lack genuine intent, raising fundamental questions about legal personhood.

news.title: WEX and Euclid AI target 90% reduction in trucking transaction costs

body.t: Elliptic AI and WEX announce a partnership to use AI for supply chain optimization in trucking.
The partnership aims to reduce transaction costs by up to 90% in the freight industry.
AI-driven automation could transform logistics, reducing costs and improving efficiency.

news.title: AI agents hacked Anthropic — maker of arguably the most capable AI models for cyberdefense

body.t: A bug bounty team used AI agents to breach Anthropic's internal systems through third-party software.
The breach affected sales, HR, and other internal systems.
This incident highlights the security risks of relying on AI agents in corporate environments.
